sanskrit: namo astu sarpebhyo ye ke ca pṛthivīm anu | ye antarikṣe ye divi tebhyaḥ sarpebhyo namaḥ ||
english: Homage be to the serpents, whoever they are throughout the earth, those in the atmosphere, those in the sky — homage to those serpents.

sanskrit: ye cāmī rocane divo ye ca sūryasya raśmiṣu | yeṣām apsu sadas kṛtaṃ tebhyaḥ sarpebhyo namaḥ ||
english: Those that are yonder in the luminous realm of heaven, those in the rays of the sun, those whose dwelling has been made in the waters — homage to those serpents.

sanskrit: yā iṣavo yātudhānānāṃ yā vā vanaspatīnām | ye 'vaṭeṣu śerate tebhyaḥ sarpebhyo namaḥ ||
english: Those that are the arrows of the sorcerers or of the forest-lords, those that lie coiled in pits — homage to those serpents.

sanskrit: yavocchiṣṭaṃ haviṣā vardhayemaṃ yathā dyumnī kṛṇavad vīryāṇī | sajūr devebhir abhi bhūḥ sapatnān āyuṣmat kṣatram ajaraṃ te astu ||
english: With the oblation of barley-remnant may we increase him so that, full of brilliance, he may achieve heroic deeds; in concert with the gods may he overcome his rivals — may undecaying sovereignty and long life be his.

sanskrit: puṃsā yavena haviṣā payasvatā- -ucchiṣṭasyāyū rakṣantu devāḥ | devā hy asmin ni dadhur nṛmṇaṃ bṛhad asmā indro vayo dadhātu ||
english: With the virile barley as a milk-rich oblation may the gods protect the life-force of the remnant; for the gods have placed great manly power in him — may Indra bestow vigour upon him.

sanskrit: sam ucchiṣṭasya haviṣā sam ukthaiḥ sam āyuṣā varcasā payo dadhātu | devā hy asmin ni dadhur nṛmṇaṃ bṛhad asmā indro vayo dadhātu ||
english: Together with the oblation of the remnant, together with the hymns of praise, together with life-force and lustre, may he bestow milk; for the gods have placed great manly power in him — may Indra bestow vigour upon him.

sanskrit: vāyur enāḥ samākarat tvaṣṭā poṣāya dhriyatām | indra ābhyo adhi bruvad rudro bhūmne cikitsatu ||
english: May Vāyu assemble them; may Tvaṣṭṛ be established for their flourishing; may Indra speak on their behalf; may Rudra attend to their abundance.

sanskrit: yathā cakrur devāsurā yathā manuṣyā uta | evā sahasrapoṣāya kṛṇutaṃ lakṣmāśvinā ||
english: Just as the gods and the asuras did it, just as humans likewise did — so, O Aśvins, produce the auspicious mark for thousandfold prosperity.

sanskrit: lohitena svadhitinā mithunaṃ karṇayoḥ kṛdhi | akartām aśvinā lakṣma tad astu prajayā bahu ||
english: With a red knife make a pair of marks on the ears; the Aśvins have made that mark — may it be plentiful through offspring.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇaṃ niyānaṃ harayaḥ suparṇā apo vasānā divam ut patanti | ā ca vartante sadanād ṛtasya- -ād id ghṛtena pṛthivī vy udyate ||
english: The tawny fair-winged ones travel the dark path, clothed in water, they fly up to heaven; and they return from the seat of cosmic order — thereupon the earth spreads open with ghee.

sanskrit: payasvatīḥ kṛṇutāpa oṣadhīr imā yad ejathā maruto rukmavakṣasaḥ | ūrjaṃ ca tatra sumatiṃ ca pinvatha yatrā naro marutaḥ siñcathā madhu ||
english: Make these waters and herbs milk-rich, O Maruts with golden breasts, when you stir; and there you swell with strength and goodwill, where, O Maruts, you men pour the sweet drink.

sanskrit: udapluto marutas tām̐ iyarta vṛṣṭyā yad viśvā nivatas pṛṇātha | ejāti galhā kanyeva tunnairun tundānā patyeva jāyā ||
english: Swollen with water, O Maruts, rouse them with rain when you fill all the valleys; the reed-grass trembles like a maiden struck, stirring like a wife toward her husband.

sanskrit: tvaṣṭeva pūṣeryo damūnā mahī svastir vṛṣaṇā na āgan | viśvā āśāḥ sūyavasā saṃrarāṇo 'syā rayyāḥ puraetā na edhi ||
english: Like Tvaṣṭṛ, like Pūṣan, the beloved of the home, great good fortune — the two bulls have come to us; rejoicing in good pastures in all directions, be for us the vanguard of this wealth.

sanskrit: eha yantu madhumad duhānā anamīvā uśatīr viśvarūpāḥ | bahvīr bhavantīr upajāyamānā ihendro vo ramayatu gāvaḥ ||
english: Let them come hither, yielding sweetness, free from disease, eager, of all forms; becoming many and multiplying — here may Indra delight you, O cows.

sanskrit: prajāpatir janayatu prajā imās tvaṣṭā dadhātu sumanasyamānaḥ | saṃvatsara ṛtubhiḥ saṃvidāno mayi puṣṭaṃ puṣṭapatir dadhātu ||
english: May Prajāpati generate these offspring; may Tvaṣṭṛ, of gracious mind, establish them; may the lord of nourishment, in concert with the seasons throughout the year, place nourishment in me.

sanskrit: sāhasī nāma vā asi sahasas pari jajñiṣe | sahasvān indro deveṣu sahase tvā khanāmasi ||
english: You are indeed named the mighty one; you were born from power. Powerful Indra is among the gods — for power we dig you up.

sanskrit: sahasyena bheṣajena divyena śataparvaṇā | tena sahasrakāṇḍena kṛṇomi punarābhṛtim ||
english: With the powerful divine remedy, the hundred-jointed one, with that thousand-stemmed plant I bring about restoration.

sanskrit: sahaso 'haṃ bheṣajasya divyasya nāma jagrabha | vy āśiṣaiva tasthire yakṣmāsaḥ puruṣād adhi ||
english: I have seized the name of the powerful divine remedy; the diseases have dispersed away from the man, as if by a blessing.

sanskrit: apeta etu nirṛtir nehāsyāḥ api kiṃ cana | apāsyāḥ satvanaḥ pāśān mṛtyūn ekaśataṃ nude ||
english: Let Nirṛti depart; let nothing of her remain here. Away from her bonds of power — the hundred deaths I drive away.

sanskrit: ye te pāśā ekaśataṃ mṛtyo martyāya hantave | tāṃs te yajñasya māyayā sarvām̐ apa yajāmasi ||
english: Your hundred snares, O Death, set to slay the mortal — all of them we worship away from you with the power of sacrifice.

sanskrit: nir ito yantu nairṛtā mṛtyava ekaśataṃ paraḥ | sedhāma eṣāṃ yat tamaḥ prāṇaṃ jyotiś ca dadhmahe ||
english: Let the hundred deaths that belong to Nirṛti depart from here, away! We drive away their darkness; we establish breath and light.

sanskrit: triṣaptā vāraṇā imās tābhir mām indro abravīt | viṣaṃ vārayatām iti viṣaṃ dūṣayatād iti ||
english: These three-times-seven repellers — with them Indra spoke to me: 'Let them ward off poison,' he said, 'let them corrupt the poison.'

sanskrit: apa brūtedaṃ maruto mahīndrasyāpavācanī | eṣā sahasram arhaty eṣā vārayate viṣam ||
english: Speak this out, O Maruts — this counter-spell of great Indra; she is worth a thousand, she wards off poison.

sanskrit: asthād dyaur asthāt pṛthivy asthād viśvam idaṃ jagat | asthur viṣasyābhītayaḥ pratikūla ivābalaḥ ||
english: Heaven has stood firm; the earth has stood firm; this entire world has stood firm; the fearlessnesses against poison have stood firm — like a feeble one facing headwinds.

sanskrit: yathā bāṇaḥ susaṃśitaḥ parāpataty āśumat | evā kāśe parā pata sākaṃ vātasya dhrājyā ||
english: Just as a well-sharpened arrow flies swiftly away — so, O reed-grass, fly away together with the rush of the wind.

sanskrit: yathā cakṣuś cakṣuṣmataḥ parāpatati ketumat | (…) sākaṃ sūryasya raśmibhiḥ ||
english: Just as the bright eye of one who has sight flies away aflame — [fly away] together with the rays of the sun.

sanskrit: yathā mano manyuketuṃ parāpatati yojanā | evā kāśe parā patat samudrasyānu vikṣaram ||
english: Just as the mind of wrathful intent flies away by leagues — so, O reed-grass, fly away along the outflow of the ocean.

sanskrit: ita evāva gacchata- -ugrā bhavata mābalāḥ | hvayantu sarve vo devāḥ sarvā vo vṛṇatāṃ viśaḥ ||
english: Go away from here, be fierce, be not weak; let all the gods summon you, let all the clans choose you.

sanskrit: yad avagamena haviṣā- -ava vo gamayāmasi | atrāta indraḥ kevalīr viśo balihṛtaḥ karat ||
english: With the oblation of the descent we send you off downward; here may Indra make the clans his own, bringing tribute.

sanskrit: indraḥ kaśyapa ād agnir iḍā turīyā vaḥ sakhā | yad bhūtaṃ bhavyam āsanvat tenāva gamayāmi vaḥ ||
english: Indra, Kaśyapa, then Agni — Iḍā is your fourth companion; with whatever has been, is, and shall be present — with that I send you off.

sanskrit: na taṃ yakṣmā arundhate nainaṃ śapatho aśnute | yaṃ bheṣajasya gulguloḥ surabhir gandho aśnute ||
english: Disease does not cling to him; the curse does not reach him — whom the fragrant odour of the bdellium remedy reaches.

sanskrit: yaṃ gulgulor bheṣajasya surabhir gandho aśnute | viṣvañcas tasmād yakṣmā mṛgā iṣvā iverate ||
english: Whom the fragrant odour of the bdellium remedy reaches — from him diseases scatter in all directions, like deer from an arrow.

sanskrit: yad gulgulu saindhavaṃ yad vā ghāsi samudriyam | ubhayor agrabhaṃ nāma- -asmā ariṣṭatātaye ||
english: What is bdellium, what is Sindhu salt, or what is the sea-herb — I have seized the name of both for his inviolability.

sanskrit: devā etaṃ madhunā saṃyutaṃ yavaṃ sarasvatyām adhi maṇāv acarkṛṣuḥ | indra āsīt sīrapatiḥ śatakratuḥ kīnāśā āsan marutaḥ sudānavaḥ ||
english: The gods ploughed this barley mixed with honey on the Sarasvatī, on the jewel-field; Indra the hundred-powered was lord of the plough; the Maruts, bountiful givers, were the ploughmen.

sanskrit: bṛhatpalāśe subhaga ūrdhvasvapna ṛtāvari | māteva putrebhyo mṛḍa keśebhyo naḥ śami ||
english: O broad-leafed one, auspicious, dreaming upward, rich in truth — be gentle to our hair as a mother to her sons; grant us welfare.

sanskrit: yas te mado +'vakeśo yo vikeśo yenābhihasyaṃ puruṣaṃ kṛṇoṣi | bhrūṇaghnovirivārā(c) cara tvaṃ tasya te prajāyāḥ suvāmi keśān ||
english: Whatever intoxication of yours causes dishevelled hair, loosened hair, by which you make a man ridiculous — you who move like one who kills an embryo from afar — from that offspring of yours I cause the hair to grow well.

sanskrit: ākūtiṃ devīṃ subhagāṃ puro dadhe cittasya mātā suhavā no astu | yām āśām emi kevalī sā me astu videyam enāṃ manasi praviṣṭām ||
english: I place the auspicious goddess of intention in the fore; may the mother of thought be easy for us to invoke. Whatever hope I pursue as my sole goal, let it be mine; may I know her as entered into the mind.

sanskrit: ākūtyā no bṛhaspata ākūtyā na upā gahi | atho bhagasya no dhehy atho naḥ suhavo bhava ||
english: O Bṛhaspati, come to us with intention, approach us with intention; then bestow Bhaga upon us, and be easy for us to invoke.

sanskrit: bṛhaspatir ma ākūtim āṅgirasaḥ prati jānātu vācam etām | yasya devā devatāḥ sambabhūvuḥ suṣupraṇīḥ kāmo anv etv asmān ||
english: May Bṛhaspati the Āṅgirasa acknowledge my intention and this speech; he of whom the gods became divinities — may Desire with its good guidance follow after us.

sanskrit: mano nv āhvāmahi nārāśaṃsena stomena | pitṝṇāṃ ca manmabhiḥ ||
english: Now let us invoke the mind with a hymn of praise to Nārāśaṃsa, and with the thoughts of the fathers.

sanskrit: ā na etu manaḥ punaḥ kratve dakṣāya jīvase | jyok ca sūryāya dṛśe ||
english: May the mind come back to us again, for will, for discernment, for living — and for long beholding of the sun.

sanskrit: punar naḥ pitaro mano dadātu daivyo janaḥ | jīvaṃ vrātaṃ sacemahi ||
english: May the fathers, the divine folk, give us back our mind; may we join the living throng.

sanskrit: vayaṃ soma vrate tava manas tanūṣu bibhrataḥ | prajāvantaḥ sacemahi ||
english: We, O Soma, in your observance, bearing mind in our bodies — may we join, possessing offspring.

sanskrit: varco me mitrāvaruṇā varco devī sarasvatī | varco me aśvinobhā dhattaṃ puṣkarasrajā ||
english: Lustre for me, O Mitra and Varuṇa; lustre, O divine Sarasvatī; both of you Aśvins, garlanded with lotuses, grant lustre to me.

sanskrit: yac ca varco yajamāne yac ca yajñe 'dhy āhitam | surāyāṃ babhru yad varcas tasya bhakṣīya varcasaḥ ||
english: Whatever lustre is placed in the sacrificer, whatever is placed in the sacrifice, whatever lustre is in the tawny sura-drink — of that lustre may I partake.

sanskrit: yā utsebhyaḥ prasravanti divo dhārā nadībhyaḥ | tāsāṃ tvā sarvāsām apām abhi ṣiñcāmi varcasā ||
english: The streams that flow down from springs, the streams of heaven, from rivers — with the lustre of all those waters I sprinkle you.

sanskrit: yad rājānaṃ śakadhūmaṃ nakṣatrāṇy akṛṇvata | bhadrāham asmai prāyacchan tato rāṣṭram ajāyata ||
english: When the constellations made Śakadhūma king, they granted him an auspicious day — from that the kingdom was born.

sanskrit: bhadrāham astu naḥ sāyaṃ bhadrāhaṃ prātar astu naḥ | bhadrāham asmabhyaṃ tvaṃ śakadhūma sadā kṛṇu ||
english: May there be an auspicious day for us in the evening; may there be an auspicious day for us in the morning; O Śakadhūma, always make an auspicious day for us.

sanskrit: yo no bhadrāham akaraḥ sāyaṃ prātar atho divā | tasmai te nakṣatrarāja śakadhūma sadā namaḥ ||
english: You who have made an auspicious day for us in the evening, in the morning, and during the day — to you, O king of constellations Śakadhūma, homage always.

sanskrit: yad āhuḥ śakadhūmāhaṃ nakṣatrāṇāṃ prathamajaṃ jyotir agre | tan naḥ saniṃ madhumatīṃ kṛṇotu rayiṃ ca naḥ sarvavīraṃ ni yacchāt ||
english: What they call the Śakadhūma day, the first-born light of the constellations at the fore — may that win for us a honey-sweet gain, and may it grant us wealth with all heroes.
